C-R5-SEARCH-ROUTING-323.Summary: Turn search results into entry points to existing work objects while preserving the search query, filters, focus and scroll position for return.
C-R5-SEARCH-ROUTING-323.Problem: The current faceted search is ACL-filtered and protects against stale responses, but every result is a passive card. Users must infer another section and find the object again. All rare filters are permanently expanded, and leaving search discards the working search context.

Goals.Goal: Return a safe route target for each accessible result after server-side ACL filtering.
Open existing meeting, plan, assignment, periodic-task, directive/science or document surfaces instead of creating search-specific detail screens.
Make the result card the primary action; keep Original as a secondary explicit link where available.
Preserve query, filter values, disclosure state, focus target and scroll position when returning to search.
Keep only search text, compact type and active filter conditions continuously visible; place rare filters behind one disclosure.
Handle stale/deleted/archived targets with an inline understandable state without bypassing ACL.

Constraints.Constraint: No SQLite migration, new search index, new detail screen, ACL relaxation or VERSION change.
The existing Action Center object router and lifecycle document inspector remain canonical and are reused.
Existing AbortController/request sequence stale-response protection remains intact.
Original is never the primary click target and does not replace the working-object route.
No animation dependency, remote asset or runtime dependency is added.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Change ranking, tokenization, FTS schema or adaptive relevance.
Add new permissions to archived or inaccessible objects.
Redesign domain cards opened from search.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Click or Enter on a meeting, plan, assignment or document result opens the exact existing domain object; periodic task, directive/science and parent routes use the same canonical router when present.
Original remains a secondary link and activating it does not trigger the primary route.
Returning with the visible К поиску action or reopening Search restores the query, every filter, advanced-filter disclosure state, scroll position and useful focus.
Only search text, compact type and active-condition chips are always visible; one disclosure contains the remaining filters on desktop and mobile.
Search API emits route metadata only after existing ACL filtering; inaccessible results remain absent.
If a routed object becomes unavailable, the search card shows an inline unavailable/archived message and the user remains in the same search context.
Existing stale-response cancellation continues to ignore superseded responses.
No motion is introduced; keyboard focus remains visible and prefers-reduced-motion behavior is unchanged.
Targeted search routing/unit/browser regression and ordinary project CI pass on one exact PR head.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Exact-head evidence proves safe route metadata, canonical object opening, primary/secondary action semantics, context restoration and compact progressive disclosure without changing search ranking or ACL.
